title: Two Teenagers Jailed 10 Years for Petrol Arson Attack on Indian Restaurant in London
excerpt: The Old Bailey heard the August 2025 attack on Indian Aroma in Gants Hill was a 'sophisticated and professional operation' that left a couple in their 20s with life-changing burns.
body:
• Two 17-year-old boys were given an extended sentence of 10 years' custody plus three years on extended licence at the Old Bailey on October 2 for the August 2025 petrol arson attack on Indian Aroma restaurant in Gants Hill, East London.
  • The attackers, armed with machetes and accompanied by a third accomplice, emptied petrol canisters over the dining room — where eight customers were eating — and set it alight, causing an "explosion."
  • A married couple in their 20s suffered life-changing burns: the woman, doused in petrol, was placed in a medically induced coma with burns to 50 percent of her body; her husband woke up 45 days later with 51 percent mixed-depth burns.
  • The judge called it a "sophisticated and professional operation" carried out "with cold blood" on the direction of an unidentified older criminal; the third accomplice has not been caught.

London: Two teenagers have been jailed for ten years over a petrol-bomb-style arson attack on an Indian restaurant in East London that left a young couple with life-changing burns.

The two 17-year-olds — whose names are withheld because of their age — were sentenced at the Old Bailey on Friday, October 2, by His Honour Judge Michael Grieve KC. Each received an extended sentence of ten years' custody followed by three years on extended licence.

The pair were convicted after a six-week trial earlier this year of arson with intent to endanger life and possessing a bladed article; one also pleaded guilty to failing to disclose a phone PIN.

The attack

On August 22, 2025, at around 9 pm, the two boys — armed with what the court heard were long knives and swords — stormed Indian Aroma on Woodford Avenue in Gants Hill/Ilford with a third accomplice. Eight customers were dining inside.

According to the prosecution case, the two guarded the door, held mostly shut, while the accomplice emptied petrol canisters onto the floor and tables — liberally spread over chairs where customers sat — then lit a slip of paper, causing an "explosion." The attackers fled in a stolen car as six London Fire Brigade vehicles responded.

Agonising injuries

A married couple in their 20s bore the worst of it. The woman was doused in petrol; her clothing melted to her skin and she was placed in a medically induced coma with burns to 50 percent of her body surface area, 45 percent of them full-thickness. Her husband was seen running out of the restaurant on fire; he woke up 45 days later with 51 percent mixed-depth burns. Two people were critically burned and four others injured.

"You did so with cold blood… the victims suffered agonising and life-changing injuries."

— His Honour Judge Michael Grieve KC, Old Bailey

Judge Grieve said the attack was a "sophisticated and professional operation" showing a "high degree" of planning, and that the offenders were "fully aware of the almost inevitable consequences… serious harm, up to and including death, to complete strangers."

He added there was "no doubt" the teenagers acted "on the direction of some older and more experienced criminal who has not been identified… but you did so with cold blood." In mitigation, one teenager argued he had been exploited in the run-up to the offence; the other claimed he had been told the restaurant would be empty.

What next

The sentencing closes one chapter, but the investigation's loose ends remain: the third accomplice who spread the petrol and lit it has not been identified or caught, and neither has the older criminal the judge said directed the operation. For London's Indian restaurant community, the case is a grim reminder of the vulnerability of small, family-run businesses — and of how close an ordinary Friday dinner service came to a mass-casualty event.
nri_angle: Indian restaurants are community anchors across the UK; an attack of this severity on a family-run eatery resonates with the million-plus Indian diaspora in Britain and its business owners.
